steps.text: Cook sausage in a large skillet over medium-high heat until browned and crumbly, 5 to 7 minutes. Transfer sausage to a plate, leaving drippings in the skillet.
Add bacon grease to the sausage drippings, and reduce the heat to medium. Whisk in flour and stir constantly until mixture becomes paste-like and turns golden brown, about 5 minutes.

Gradually whisk in milk until smooth. Bring to a simmer, then return sausage to the skillet and season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until mixture is smooth and thick, 10 to 15 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Old-Fashioned Sausage Gravy
raw_recipe.description: Old-fashioned sausage gravy featuring pork sausage cooked in bacon fat. A roux is made with the drippings for a gravy that you'll want on repeat.
raw_recipe.name: Old-Fashioned Sausage Gravy

review.reviewBody: This is a great recipe for sausage gravy. I do make mine slightly different though. First, I don't add the bacon grease because I feel mine has more than enough. With the sausage in the pan I will add the flour, then the milk and spices. I also really prefer mine with sage sausage to give it a little more flavor. Maple sausage doesn't taste quite right though.

I made this recipe with 4 TBSP bacon grease and Butterball Taco Seasoned Turkey Sausage, which I drained before returning to the skillet. There is a VIP in my life who thinks I’m marvelous because I can make country sausage gravy, my Grandson, who thinks I am a genius because I make sausage gravy so quickly. Another item added, a cup of additional milk cup of additional plllit was a little thicker than he likes his gravy. Additionally, I drained the turkey sausage on a dinner plate with 2 whole sheets of paper towels underneath! The base recipe is exceptionally done, and I make it for myself just as stated in the recipe. It is possible that you will like it either way.——MaggieMae4ever/Fort Worth

Very easy and basic recipe. I didn't have bacon grease and was hoping I wouldn't need any, but I did need some extra grease, so I added about 1-1/2 T of vegetable shortening. Whenever I cook ground beef or pork, I always chop an onion for added flavor, so I added that here and cooked it with the pork, additionally, I added some salt, pepper and sage while cooking the pork for a little extra flavor. I also fried some eggs to serve with for those who wanted. Thanks for the simple and fulfilling recipe. BTW - had no trouble feeding a family of four with two teens. Plenty of food.

I rated this 5 stars even though I'm one of "those" ppl that add some extra seasonings, etc. This is a great base for standard sausage gravy though! It all depends on what kind of sausage you use as well. I generally use Tennessee Pride Sage flavor in a roll. I remove the cooked sausage and press the grease out through a mesh strainer back into the skillet (cast iron of course). I wind up sauteing a couple Tblsp of minced onion in the grease and cook the flour in that until it's a nice light tan color. I normally only add 1 T of bacon grease to have enough for the roux process. I like to add a bit of thyme, grnd coriander, grated nutmeg and a sprinkle of cayenne pepper. I add back in however much of the cooked sausage I'm in the mood for. Sometimes all if it, sometimes only half. Either way I freeze any leftovers and it works alright for me. The recipe as written is good; add more "stuff" if you want a lil more flavor :)

I had to use turkey sausage, so the recipe needed a little help. 2 tbs olive oil 1lb turkey sausage 1 tbs sage 2tsp oregano 1 tsp minced garlic 2 tbs salted butter 1/4 c a.p. flour 1.5 c milk 1/2 tsp salt 1/2 tsp pepper 4 drops Louisiana Hot Sauce

Delish! I've made "my own" sausage gravy for years by the old throw some flour in with the sausage and then add milk and this is basically what this is. I had never added bacon drippings though. I tripled the recipe and got a little heavy handed with the bacon drippings so though a good gravy, the bacon flavor was more prominent than I'd have liked. Not bad flavor, but not as sausagey. I use Tennesee Pride sausage and it's rather mild so used a good half a palmful of sage and as other readers commented, the sage really added some good flavor. I had some evaporated milk that needed to be used to I threw that in along with my skim milk and it bumped up the creamyness and flavor. All in all, this is a keeper. Hubby enjoyed it for brunch and just came back (it's 7:30 PM) and just grabbed a bowl of it. The rest will go in the freezer for an quick meal another day.

The recipe was good but not the best I've had. I would not add 3 T of bacon grease. 2 T would be enough (maybe even 1 T would be enough). The bacon grease does add to the flavor so don't forget it (butter isn't the same). Also, I would add about 1/4 to 1/2 t. of a spice (thyme, sage (my favorite) or rosemary) or use sage sausage to give it a little more flavor. I also cook my sausage pretty dark as another tester said. This recipe is very easy to make. However, like another tester said, it definitely doesn't make 8 servings--more like 2.5. It is definitely good though. (I needed to add a little more milk to make it less thick.) Sure is easy to make, and the gravy is not lumpy or greasy. (It is definitely all the grease/fat you'll want in a day, but you don't eat biscuits and gravy for health reasons. You eat it for pleasure!) *G* Use Big Daddy's Biscuits with this. You'll love the results!

Sausage gravy is so simple... This recipe is with a little extra work. Brown the sausage, (really dark) If you can get a few hunks very dark, the better. If you have grease in the bottom of your skillet, do not add bacon grease. I use Oldhams sausage and it is very dry. Add flour and then cook and stir until the flour is turning just tan in color. In the mean time get the bowl you want to serve the gravy in and fill it almost full of milk. When the sausage is ready, turn up the heat and add milk. Stir constantly, until thick. Use a cold spoon and dip it into the gravy and taste it for thickness and spices.

Lots of flavor, but takes a lot longer to thicken than my method of about half milk and half cream all in the same pan as the sausage. I do think I'll incorporate the bacon grease for flavor like the recipe calls for though.

I loved this! I made this for my husband, my 15 yr old son, and his two friends. They all came back for seconds and thirds! I used Jimmy Dean sausage which left almost no grease, so the bacon grease was a must. Also, I added a little more flour because I like a thicker gravy. At the end I felt it needed more flavor (maybe because of the lack of sausage grease, I don't know), so I added some seasoning salt along with fresh ground black pepper. The seasoning salt was the trick. It tasted great! To reheat, just put it back in a pan, add a little milk or cream, and stir. Thanks for such a great recipe!
Awesome! Next time I'll only use 2 tbsp of (flavored) bacon grease. I felt it could use a little seasoning, so to avoid over-salting I added a pinch of Accent while it simmered.
I made the recipe just as written. First time I have managed to make good gravy. Definitely a keeper
Regular Sunday breakfast for my family. Taste way better then any diner or cafe.
The only thing I changed was adding half a yellow onion and using brats that were leftover from a barbecue. I'll definitely make this again
Easy and delicious. I served it over noodles, but you can do biscuits, or really anything... everyone in my house loved it.
This was my first time making this recipe and it was a huge fail. Ended up having to go buy store gravy.
Love this recipe!
Great recipe easy to follow. The only modification i mad was i halfed the bacon grease for health reasons.
I really like the flavor of this gravy. It was quite easy to make and has a good old fashioned hearty taste.
Easy to make and the family LOVED it!
